scope_notes: security-tool profile: an autonomous, code-executing AI pentest agent run with Docker; uses_crypto set true (AES-256 report encryption, PKCE, HMAC, cryptography dep) which the probe missed, adding SEC-9; heavy_compute false (LLM inference is remote).

PUR-1.note: README states problem, users (incl. agents), quickstart, exit codes/artifacts and an authorized-use warning; no machine-readable capability statement.

PUR-2.note: Only headline cited is XBEN 96% for v0.4.0 (repo at 1.7.0); harness+raw results live in external usestrix/benchmarks, none committed here, so not reproducible at this commit.

PUR-3.note: Large surface (TUI+React viewer bundle+cloud CLI 138 cmds); components have documented reasons but no necessity gate or tracked surface size.

COR-1.note: 131 py + 17 go test files, test/source 0.665; CI runs pytest (3.12-3.14), go test -race, viewer build, wheel/binary smoke; ci-passed gate. No coverage measurement/threshold.

COR-2.note: Oracles are internal (Go/Python protocol-constant parity, SARIF schema, packaging asserts); no independent answer key/golden for the model-dependent security findings.

COR-3.note: No mutation/property/fuzz testing in host code (no hypothesis/atheris; probe fuzz=0 files, refs are docs); untrusted-input parsers have malformed-input unit tests + a depth cap but no fuzzing.

COR-4.note: CI installs the wheel into a clean env and runs the CLI, and runs a real quick scan to check provider-credential wiring; no self-scan of strix's own code and no tracked findings.

COR-5.note: LLM-driven output is inherently nondeterministic; run/finding ids are sequential/uuid and SARIF partialFingerprints give cross-run stickiness, but nondeterminism is not documented or isolated by seeds.

REL-1.note: --resume rehydrates root + non-terminal subagents' full LLM history and agent topology from strix_runs (run.json + SQLite sessions, atomic writes); kill/interrupt-and-resume is tested. Tool side effects are not idempotent on replay.

REL-2.note: Tool outputs capped by bytes/lines/tokens with spill-to-disk + context auto-compact; sandbox json-log capped on by default; optional cgroup mem/cpu/pids caps; USD and turn budgets.

REL-3.note: coverage.json marks complete:false with caveats and SARIF sets executionSuccessful:false on a truncated run; transient model failures retry with bounded backoff.

REL-4.note: SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP handlers + atexit cleanup; sandbox container best-effort killed on delete; teardown settles live children before closing sessions, with tests.

PERF-1.note: External XBEN notes ~19 min/solve and cost; no in-repo latency harness or per-operation budgets; per-call timing only via optional STRIX_RUN_RECORD_TIMINGS.

PERF-2.note: Summary-first tool outputs with disk-spill retrieval handles, model-aware context budget and auto-compaction; ~44 base agent tools. Catalog/per-answer token cost not measured.

SEC-1.note: No SECURITY.md, no threat-model/trust-boundary doc and no vulnerability-disclosure contact for a code-executing autonomous security tool; README carries only an authorized-use warning. Red-line SEC checked: no committed secrets (SEC-6) and no injection-prone host patterns (SEC-7).

SEC-2.note: Lockfiles for py/go/npm; dependabot across 4 ecosystems with cooldown; bandit SAST in CI. No known-vulnerability dependency scanner gates repo CI (govulncheck/trivy/trufflehog listed by the probe are tools inside the sandbox image, not repo CI).

SEC-3.note: Releases build in CI across 5 platforms but carry no provenance/attestation or signing; GitHub release just uploads artifacts with auto notes.

SEC-4.note: No SBOM generation in CI and no NOTICE/third-party license file, though the wheel bundles a Go sidecar and a prebuilt React viewer.

SEC-5.note: All 24 third-party action refs pinned by full SHA; every workflow sets least-privilege top-level permissions (contents:read), release job scopes contents:write; no pull_request_target; zizmor + actionlint gates; persist-credentials:false.

SEC-6.note: RED LINE: not triggered. No secrets committed outside tests (independently confirmed); stored credentials written 0600; bandit in CI/pre-commit. Weaker than horizon: no secret scanner in repo CI and no tested redaction of agent-visible outputs.

SEC-7.note: RED LINE: not triggered. Host Python/Go free of shell-string/eval/unsafe-deserialization/TLS-off on untrusted paths (subprocess uses list args). The 4 dangerouslySetInnerHTML sites render hljs-escaped/entity-escaped content in the loopback-only viewer.

SEC-8.note: Untrusted API specs parsed in memory-safe Python with yaml.safe_load, a recursion-depth cap and malformed-input tests; untrusted target/web content is handled inside the Docker sandbox. No continuous fuzzing of the parsers.

SEC-9.note: uses_crypto set true: PKCE S256, AES-256 report encryption (pypdf), hmac.compare_digest, secrets tokens, cryptography>=48 dep. No deprecated algorithms, but no algorithm inventory, abstraction layer or PQC migration plan.

AGT-1.note: Untrusted target content (the agent's input by design) is run inside an isolated sandbox and some surfaces are labelled (Caido error pages 'NOT RESPONSES FROM THE TARGET'), but instruction/data channels are not separated in prompts and there is no injection-resistance regression corpus.

AGT-2.note: Agent runs with broad in-sandbox power by design (NET_ADMIN/NET_RAW, passwordless sudo inside the container); no per-tool readOnly/destructive machine hints; scope authorization is limited to declared target base URLs with no deny-by-default egress.

AGT-3.note: Interactive TUI shows a live action view, supports steering, wait_for_user and Ctrl-C stop; run.json/request_log are a readable action log; budgets stop runs. Exploit actions are not reversible (inherent).

AGT-4.note: No in-repo evaluation suite run when models/prompts/providers change; the only eval is the external XBEN benchmark. A model is used for finding dedupe without a regression eval.

AGT-5.note: Providers/models documented and recommended models listed; reports are stamped 'Generated' with a timestamp but not marked AI-generated, and there is no model/data card or AI-BOM.

AGT-6.note: Per-run USD budget (cumulative, graduated warnings, sub-agent reserve), per-agent turn cap and max tool calls per turn; cost/usage recorded in run.json and beacons.

INT-1.note: CLI with JSON output, an MCP client, a cloud REST CLI mirroring a published OpenAPI, and SARIF 2.1.0 output; no stated version/compatibility policy for the CLI contract.

INT-2.note: Nine SKILL.md packs, --help and JSON/SARIF output give partial self-description; no describe --json manifest of commands/inputs/outputs/effects and no contract-vs-code drift check.

INT-3.note: ~44 composable base agent tools (reasonable); the 138-command cloud CLI is large but is a declarative 1:1 mirror of REST verbs rather than bespoke tools.

INT-4.note: Cloud CLI has stable exit codes (0/1/2/4/5), next_step hints and JSON error payloads; MCP failures carry a typed kind with a correct retryable flag. Agent in-sandbox tool errors are free-text strings.

INT-5.note: Cloud mutations take stable idempotency keys bound to actor+body (tested); source uploads are approved by archive sha256; run names and vuln-NNNN ids are stable; SARIF fingerprints address findings.

INT-6.note: Quickstart is exercised by the packaging smoke and --help is complete; the React viewer has 76 a11y attributes but no accessibility tooling/tests and no internationalisation.

INT-7.note: Results exported on disk as SARIF 2.1.0, vulnerabilities.json, run.json and markdown report; open, documented, third-party-readable formats.

EPI-1.note: Findings carry evidence, PoC, counterevidence and confidence; run.json records model/usage/version; coverage.json separates agent_reported from machine_observed provenance; SARIF carries tool version + fingerprints.

EPI-2.note: Findings require a confidence class (high/medium/low) with a mandatory rationale when below high, plus counterevidence and severity-change conditions; coverage marks surfaces 'unexamined, not clean'.

EPI-3.note: coverage.json explicitly distinguishes 'tested, nothing found' from 'never looked', reports gaps, and a truncated run is stamped incomplete rather than clean.

EPI-4.note: coverage.json reconciles declared scope, surfaces reviewed, skill-implied gaps and completeness caveats, with machine-observed facts that contradict (not confirm) the agent's ledger; surfaced into SARIF. Not CI-gated for reconciliation of declared questions.

EPI-5.note: RED LINE: not triggered (no in-repo measurement contradicts a headline). But claims lean on superlatives and an external, stale (v0.4.0) benchmark, and configuration docs describe OTEL/Traceloop + events.jsonl that are absent from the shipped code.

MNT-1.note: Package layout (agents/tools/runtime/report/interface) is documented, but there are no enforced architecture/import boundary rules.

MNT-2.note: Largest source file 2603 lines; 0 duplicate files; ruff enables eradicate (ERA) for dead code; no dedicated duplication/dead-code budget enforced.

MNT-3.note: ruff (large rule set) + mypy strict + pyright strict + bandit configured and run in CI; gofmt/go vet/go test -race for the TUI; tsconfig strict for the viewer.

MNT-4.note: CONTRIBUTING, AGENTS.md, a docs site and nine SKILL.md packs are present and current; no architecture decision records.

MNT-5.note: Zero TODO/FIXME markers and detailed lint-ignore rationales, but no debt ledger and at least one hidden drift: docker_client.py claims 'Pinned to openai-agents==0.14.6' while uv.lock pins 0.19.0.

EVO-1.note: Version 1.7.0 declared; no committed CHANGELOG, no stated SemVer/migration policy, and GitHub auto-generated notes are the only release record.

EVO-2.note: Release workflow builds, asserts wheel/binary shape and runs --version across platforms, but there is no changelog or documented qualification record, so cadence is not absorbable from the repo.

EVO-3.note: Release matrix covers macOS arm64+x86_64, linux x86_64+arm64 and Windows; CI tests Python 3.12-3.14; requires-python and Go 1.24 stated and enforced in builds.

EVO-4.note: No support period, EOL policy or security-update window is stated for a distributed product (EU CRA support-period obligation).

OPS-1.note: Startup validation checks model/API-key/Docker and prints actionable fixes, but there is no dedicated, separately-invokable doctor/self-check command and coverage is narrow.

OPS-2.note: Logging carries contextual scan_id/agent_id fields with configurable levels, but logs are not structured JSON and there are no metrics; the OTEL/Traceloop tracing described in the docs is not implemented in this repo.

OPS-3.note: pydantic-settings validates types at load and loopback viewer bind is a safe default, but ~22 of 28 env vars are undocumented and telemetry defaults on (not the safe default).

OPS-4.note: Primary install is curl|bash and the installer downloads the release binary with no checksum or signature verification; pipx/uv/pip paths exist but are not the headline.

PRV-1.note: RED LINE: not triggered. Telemetry is on by default but disclosed (telemetry/README.md, configuration docs), anonymised with a random session id and no user content ($process_person_profile false). Below meets: no DO_NOT_TRACK support and no prominent first-run notice.

PRV-2.note: Local-first: scans run in local Docker, results stay on disk, viewer 'nothing leaves your machine'; telemetry is content-free and the managed cloud is a separate opt-in. No explicit deletion/export tooling beyond on-disk files.

PRV-3.note: RED LINE: not triggered. Apache-2.0 LICENSE present with the SPDX id in pyproject; but there is no NOTICE/third-party notices file despite bundling a Go sidecar, a React viewer and many dependencies.

PRV-4.note: No stated regulatory position for strix itself; the regulation mentions in docs are about producing SOC2/ISO/PCI reports for customers, not strix's own EU CRA / AI-Act posture as a distributed autonomous agent.

SUS-1.note: No CODEOWNERS and no governance/succession doc; company-backed (usestrix) but repo governance and maintainer breadth are not evidenced (shallow clone).

SUS-2.note: Issue templates, a required ci-passed gate aggregating all lanes, a documented PR process and a pre-commit config.

SUS-3.note: AGENTS.md and SKILL.md support agents using strix, but neither CONTRIBUTING nor AGENTS states a policy for how AI-authored contributions to this repo are reviewed or attributed.

gaps.title: No security policy, threat model or disclosure channel
gaps.case: No SECURITY.md anywhere in the repo (meta.security_policy found=false); README.md:385 carries only an authorized-use warning.
gaps.impact: governance / coordinated-vulnerability-handling: a code-executing security tool has no coordinated-disclosure path or stated trust boundaries (EU CRA gap).
gaps.fix: Add SECURITY.md with a disclosure contact and response targets, publish advisories (GHSA), and commit a threat-model/trust-boundary section.

gaps.title: Unverified install and unattested releases
gaps.case: README.md:84 and scripts/install.sh:154 fetch the release binary over curl|bash with no checksum/signature check; build-release.yml:100 uploads artifacts with no provenance/signing (ci.provenance found=false).
gaps.impact: supply chain: tampering with the installer or release artifacts of a tool that then runs with Docker and broad in-sandbox privileges.
gaps.fix: Publish signed artifacts with build provenance (Sigstore/SLSA) and make the installer verify a checksum or signature.

gaps.title: Documentation describes observability the code does not ship
gaps.case: docs/advanced/configuration.mdx:148-166 documents TRACELOOP/OTEL remote tracing and a local events.jsonl, but no OTEL/Traceloop/events.jsonl implementation exists in strix/ (grep).
gaps.impact: epistemic: operators relying on the documented audit/trace trail get nothing, and the doc overstates shipped capability.
gaps.fix: Ship the OTEL export and events.jsonl, or remove the documentation until it is implemented in this repo.

gaps.title: Headline capability number is external and stale
gaps.case: benchmarks/README.md:24 cites a 96% XBEN result for Strix v0.4.0 while pyproject.toml:3 is 1.7.0; the harness and raw results live in an external repo (benchmarks/README.md:8), none committed here.
gaps.impact: epistemic: the flagship capability claim cannot be reproduced at the reviewed commit and is tied to an old version.
gaps.fix: Commit the harness and raw results (or a slim answer-key lane) and re-run it against the shipped version, dated.

gaps.title: No SBOM, VEX or third-party notices for a distributed bundle
gaps.case: No SBOM step in CI (ci.sbom found=false) and no NOTICE/third-party license file (meta.notices found=false), though the wheel bundles a Go sidecar and a prebuilt React viewer.
gaps.impact: compliance: EU CRA SBOM obligation (Dec 2027) unmet and third-party attribution debt.
gaps.fix: Generate a CycloneDX/SPDX SBOM per release and add a complete NOTICE file.

gaps.title: Untrusted-input parsers are not fuzzed
gaps.case: strix/utils/api_spec.py parses attacker-influenceable OpenAPI/Swagger/Postman specs; it has malformed-input unit tests (tests/test_api_spec.py:121) and a depth cap but no fuzzing, and there is no mutation/property testing anywhere (COR-3).
gaps.impact: correctness/robustness: parser edge cases on hostile input are unverified.
gaps.fix: Add fuzz targets for the spec parser and the other untrusted-input readers with size/recursion assertions.

gaps.title: Untrusted target content is not separated from instructions
gaps.case: The agent is designed to act on target-controlled content, but strix/agents/prompts/system_prompt.jinja does not mark an untrusted_content channel distinct from instructions, and there is no injection-resistance regression suite (agent.prompt_injection refs are sandbox/isolation, not channel separation).
gaps.impact: AI safety: an autonomous agent can be steered by instructions embedded in target content; mitigation currently rests on prompt wording, not a policy boundary.
gaps.fix: Label untrusted channels explicitly and add a held-out injection regression corpus run per model version (defensive, no technique detail needed).

gaps.title: Cryptography has no inventory, abstraction or PQC plan
gaps.case: AES-256 report encryption (strix/interface/viewer/report_pdf.py:679), PKCE S256 (strix/config/codex.py:169) and HMAC (sidecar) are used directly with no algorithm inventory, replaceable layer or post-quantum plan.
gaps.impact: horizon/compliance: CNSA 2.0 and the NIST 2030-35 transition are unprepared.
gaps.fix: Document a crypto inventory, route crypto through one abstraction, and publish a dated ML-KEM/ML-DSA migration plan.

gaps.title: No support period, changelog or SemVer policy
gaps.case: No committed CHANGELOG, no stated SemVer/migration policy (evo.semver) and no support/EOL window (evo.support found=false) for a PyPI-distributed product.
gaps.impact: evolution/compliance: downstreams cannot pin on compatibility or on a security-fix window (EU CRA support-period).
gaps.fix: Add a CHANGELOG with migration notes, state a SemVer policy and declare a support period.

opportunities.title: Extract the coverage-accounting record as a shared standard
opportunities.description: coverage.json separates declared scope, tested-clean, unexamined gaps and completeness caveats, and keeps agent-reported apart from machine-observed facts that contradict it. It is a self-contained, high-value artifact (dissection score 18) that rea (residual unknowns) and caveman could consume as a common coverage-record format.

opportunities.title: Bound agent egress with agent-sandbox-lockdown's allowlist
opportunities.description: The strix sandbox grants NET_ADMIN/NET_RAW with no deny-by-default egress (its own report prose recommends one). Composing with agent-sandbox-lockdown's CoreDNS + tinyproxy deny-by-default allowlist would bound what an autonomous pentest agent can reach to the authorized scope.

opportunities.title: Route tool outputs through caveman's compressors + CCR
opportunities.description: strix already spills oversized tool output to disk and retrieves it by path; caveman's byte-safe S0-S4 compressors and content-addressed CCR recovery handles would cut agent context cost further while keeping byte-exact recovery, sharing a retrieval-handle shape.

opportunities.title: Turn the report pipeline into a CRA/AI-Act evidence pipeline
opportunities.description: strix already emits SARIF 2.1.0 and coverage completeness and sells compliance-ready reports; adding SBOM/VEX and an AI-BOM to the release and report pipeline makes it a dated-obligation-ready output customers will need by 2027.

opportunities.title: Commit a reproducible benchmark lane with bench hygiene
opportunities.description: Bring the XBEN harness (or a slim answer-key) in-repo and run it per release with ponytail-style bench hygiene (interleaved arms, reps, CI), so the headline number is versioned and reproducible instead of external and stale.

reengineering.gain: tamper-evident distribution for a privileged tool
reengineering.measure: release carries a provenance attestation and signature, installer verifies a checksum/signature, and an SBOM is attached per release

reengineering.gain: coordinated disclosure path and EU-CRA readiness
reengineering.measure: SECURITY.md with contact + response targets committed, a threat-model doc present, and an advisory process (GHSA) in place

reengineering.gain: a reusable coverage-record standard across the reviewed tools
reengineering.measure: a versioned schema is published and consumed by at least one other repository

reengineering.gain: agent reachability bounded to authorized scope
reengineering.measure: a deny-by-default egress allowlist is enforced for the sandbox and covered by a test

questions: Does strix commit live secrets or leak them in logs/outputs (SEC-6 red line)? No: no secrets outside tests, stored credentials are 0600, and bandit runs in CI/pre-commit; not a red line.

Are there injection-prone operations on untrusted paths in host code (SEC-7 red line)? No: host Python/Go avoid shell-strings/eval/unsafe-deserialization/TLS-off (subprocess uses list args); the viewer's dangerouslySetInnerHTML sites render escaped/highlighted content on a loopback-only server; not a red line.

Are headline/benchmark claims contradicted by an in-repo measurement (EPI-5 red line)? No in-repo measurement exists to contradict; the claims are external-cited, stale (v0.4.0) or documentation of unshipped features, so EPI-5 is 2, not 0.
not_examined: Runtime behaviour (static review only; nothing was executed)
The external usestrix/benchmarks repo that holds the XBEN harness and raw results
The managed app.strix.ai cloud backend and enterprise features
The Kali sandbox image contents beyond containers/Dockerfile
Git history and contributor breadth (shallow clone, single commit read)
